neighbours.label: ' off' meaning away from or down from, after a verb of motion ('fell off the', 'hopped off his', 'stepped off', 'got off to a start'); particle 'off' in 'turn off', 'cut off', 'paid off' stays quiet (the scan also shows 'cko' of 'gecko')
fire: The vase slid off the shelf during the earthquake.
A boy leapt off the pier into the cold lake.
The rider climbed off her horse and tied it to the fence.
Our holiday got off to a terrible start at the airport.
The lid rolled off the counter and under the fridge.
Two passengers stepped off the train at the last stop.
The kitten tumbled off the sofa and landed on a cushion.
He jumped off the ladder before it could tip over.
quiet: The guard switched off the alarm during the earthquake.
A boy showed off his new watch by the cold lake.
The rider called off the race and tied her horse to the fence.
Our gamble paid off in the end at the auction.
The plumber shut off the water under the fridge.
Two passengers dozed off on the train before the last stop.
The storm cut off the village and flooded the road.
He wrote off the debt before it could grow.

notes: Card: ' off' x19 of the top 32, plus ' Gecko'/'cko' x7. Probes: jumped off 1.04, got off to 0.80 and 0.76, hopped off 0.74, fell off 0.68, stepped off 0.54, kicked off 0.20; turned off 0.00, cut off 0.01, paid off 0.01, took off (plane) 0.02, 20% off 0.04, keep off 0.07; gecko 0.89.
